dublinCore.dc:title: 118 HR 8628 IH: Examining Consumer Choice in Digital Payments Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Donalds introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services

form.official-title: To prohibit the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection from issuing new rules or guidance relating to buy now pay later services until the Bureau and the Comptroller General of the United States each conduct a study on such services, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Examining Consumer Choice in Digital Payments Act.

section.header: Prohibition on issuing new rules or guidance relating to buy now pay later services until completion of studies

subsection.text: The Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection may not issue any new rule or guidance relating to buy now pay later services until—

paragraph.text: after the reports required under subsections (b)(2) and (c)(2) are submitted to the relevant congressional committees; and
the Bureau has considered the results of such reports with respect to such new rule or guidance.
The Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection shall conduct a study on buy now pay later services to determine—

subparagraph.text: the nature, size, and role of the entities offering buy now pay later services;
the market share held by the primary nonbank firms and financial institutions offering buy now pay later services;
the demographics of consumers most likely to utilize buy now pay later services and for what purpose;
the disclosures provided to consumers regarding buy now pay later services, including the accessibility and readability of such disclosures;
the benefits of buy now pay later services, including—

clause.text: the potential for increased purchasing power; and

subparagraph.text: the risks of buy now pay later services, including—

clause.text: potential for delinquencies and prolonged debt;
the ability of consumer reporting agencies to accurately score buy now pay later transactions; and
any unintended consequences for reporting data on such services to consumer reporting agencies;

subparagraph.text: the prevalence of partnerships between entities offering buy now pay later services and traditional financial institutions and e-commerce platforms; and
the potential for fraud in buy now pay later services.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection shall submit to the relevant congressional committees a report that includes the results of the study required by paragraph (1).

subsection.text: The Comptroller General of the United States shall—

paragraph.text: conduct a study on buy now pay later services—

subparagraph.text: to determine the information specified in subparagraphs (A) through (H) of subsection (b)(1); and
that compares the specific features, benefits, and risks of using such services to the use of other products, including—

clause.text: the average interest rate charged to consumers;
the range of interest rates charged to consumers;
the amount and type of fees charged to consumers annually;
the clarity of legal disclosures associated with such use; and
consumer understanding of payment cycles and due dates; and

paragraph.text: not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, submit to the relevant congressional committees a report that includes the results of the study required by paragraph (1).

subsection.text: The Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection shall withdrawn the interpretive rule titled Truth in Lending (Regulation Z); Use of Digital User Accounts to Access Buy Now, Pay Later Loans (May 22, 2024), and such interpretive rule shall have no force or effect.

paragraph.text: The term buy now pay later services means an alternative payment method that allows consumers to pay for purchases in up to 4 installments.
The term relevant congressional committees means—

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate.
